decisive_items: Bacterial colonies observed in submucosa surrounding the ESD lesion.
Ascites culture yielded growth of Escherichia coli.
diffuse tenderness with rebound tenderness, primarily in the right abdomen
response.rationale: Post-procedure peritonitis is best supported by bacterial invasion at the ESD site, E. coli ascites, and evolving rebound tenderness. Typhlitis lacks a clear procedure link and severe neutropenia; perforated appendicitis is contradicted by CT showing no perforation and by ascending colon localization.

rejected.why: Typhlitis is unlikely because the patient is not severely neutropenic and the findings center on the ESD lesion in the ascending colon rather than spontaneous cecal typhlitis.
Perforated appendicitis is contradicted by CT showing no intestinal perforation and by imaging/histology localizing the process to the ascending colon ESD site, not the appendix.
